chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna, from Abu Baseer, who said:

A man asked him (peace be upon him) and I was listening. He said: 'Can I give the zakat of my wealth to my relatives while they do not recognize (the Wilayah)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not give the zakat except to a Muslim (who recognizes the Wilayah), and give them from your wealth other than the zakat.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you think that only the zakat is in the wealth? What Allah has imposed in the wealth other than the zakat is more. You give from it to the relatives and the objectors among those who ask you, so you give to them as long as you do not recognize them as Nasibi (hostile). So when you recognize them as Nasibi, do not give to them except if you fear their tongue, so you buy your religion and your honor from them.'

key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: Muslim (in the context of recognizing Wilayah)

ai.seo_question: Can I give Zakat to my relatives who are not Shia or do not recognize the Wilayah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the religious obligation of Zakat, which requires specific faith criteria (excluding the Nasibi), and voluntary charity (Sadaqah), which can be given to relatives regardless of their status. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'Nasabiyyah' (hostility to the Imams) disqualifies one from receiving Zakat, while also emphasizing the practical wisdom of giving from one's own wealth to maintain familial ties and avoid the harm of a hostile tongue.
